title: Maité A. Barrena
text:
I’m a marine ecologist (she/her) finishing my PhD at the National University of Comahue and a doctoral fellow at CIMAS–CONICET in San Antonio Oeste, northern Patagonia, Argentina.
My research looks at how coastal fish and invertebrate assemblages of San Antonio Bay change through space and time, and how they relate to trophic interactions and artisanal fisheries. I use Patagonian coastal systems as a natural laboratory.
I care deeply about making ecological research reproducible, transparent and reusable. I trained as an open science instructor at the LMU Open Science Center, I work on research data stewardship, and I’m moving toward metascience in marine ecology: studying how we collect, report and share ecological data.
I also teach mathematics to marine biology students.

title: Open Science & Research Data
text: Ecology relies more and more on long-term monitoring, satellite products and large shared datasets. Whether those data can be found, understood and reused depends on how we organise, document and report our work. I want to help close that gap in marine ecology, both by teaching practical workflows and by studying research practices themselves (metascience).
